formula: integral_gamma f(z) d z=integral_a^b f(gamma(t))gamma'(t)d t
text: A contour integral adds changes along a directed path. Parameterize the path by a real variable t. Multiply the function value by the complex velocity of the path, then integrate in t; both path shape and orientation are accounted for.
title: Idea 1

text: For the function z, an antiderivative is z squared divided by two. Every piecewise smooth path from zero to one plus i therefore gives i. The endpoint formula follows because this antiderivative exists throughout the region containing the path.
title: Idea 2

formula: z=e^(i t), quad frac(1,z)frac(d z,d t)=i
text: Now travel counterclockwise around the unit circle while integrating one over z. The path velocity is i times z, so the product simplifies to i. Integrating from zero to two pi gives two pi i, not zero.
title: Idea 3

text: There is no contradiction with Cauchy's theorem: one over z is undefined at the enclosed origin. A holomorphic function on an open region containing the whole disk has zero integral around its boundary. Enclosed singularities change the situation.
title: Idea 4
